name: Familial Mitral Valve Prolapse

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Mitral Valve Prolapse

criteria.description: Systolic displacement of one or both mitral valve leaflets >2 mm beyond the mitral annulus in parasternal long-axis view
Mitral leaflet thickening ≥5 mm during diastole
Presence of mitral valve prolapse in first-degree relatives

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of systolic leaflet displacement >2 mm beyond the mitral annulus with or without leaflet thickening, supported by family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings; genetic testing may support diagnosis in familial cases.

pathognomonic.notes: Audible on auscultation, characteristic of mitral valve prolapse

pathognomonic.symptomName: Late systolic murmur of mitral regurgitation
pathognomonic.notes: Heard best at the cardiac apex
searchTerms: heart murmur from mitral valve leakage

common.notes: Commonly premature ventricular contractions or atrial arrhythmias
Due to mitral regurgitation or reduced cardiac output

common.symptomName: Chest discomfort or atypical chest pain
searchTerms: chest discomfort or unusual chest pain

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to decreased cardiac efficiency
searchTerms: fatigue due to decreased cardiac output
low energy related to heart inefficiency

occasional.notes: May be related to autonomic dysfunction
Reported in some patients with MVP syndrome
Rare but may indicate arrhythmogenic risk
Due to mitral regurgitation or arrhythmias

rare.notes: Complication in patients with significant valve abnormalities
Secondary to emboli from mitral valve thrombi
searchTerms: brain stroke or blood clot traveling in body
stroke or systemic blood clot event

rare.symptomName: Severe mitral regurgitation leading to heart failure
searchTerms: severe leaking mitral valve causing heart failure
mitral valve disease with fluid buildup

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; inflammatory markers may be elevated if endocarditis develops
imaging: Echocardiography showing leaflet prolapse and mitral regurgitation
Doppler studies assessing severity of regurgitation
Cardiac MRI for detailed valve and ventricular assessment
genetic: Familial clustering with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Electrocardiogram may show arrhythmias or repolarization abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Often sporadic or associated with connective tissue disorders
Systemic connective tissue manifestations (e.g. tall stature, lens dislocation)
Genetic testing positive for FBN1 mutations

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe mitral regurgitation symptoms
Signs of infective endocarditis (fever, new murmur, embolic phenomena)
references: Nishimura RA, et al. 2020 AHA/ACC Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease. Circulation. 2020.
Freeman RV, et al. Familial clustering of mitral valve prolapse in the community. Circulation. 2000.
Delling FN, et al. Genetics and pathophysiology of mitral valve prolapse. Curr Opin Cardiol. 2015.
